lines: So here's what this topic's own two small boundaries are really standing in for: a real extension built this way isn't limited to handing Python back a brand new answer every time.
It can hand Python the exact same memory it was already holding, and it can step out of the interpreter's own way entirely while it does the real work underneath.
Neither one happens automatically; both are a real, explicit choice the code has to make, the same way the handle, the status code, and the unwind boundary were.
And that's the real thread running through this entire chapter: crossing out of Rust was never going to be automatic, not once, not anywhere along the way.
